ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first: the whole chat (F9 stop request at 14:17, F10 driver's "Sure"), the driver's post-trip statement F12 and the rider's complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the words read as an ordinary parcel-stop request and a fare complaint [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Safety_concern is therefore "none".

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so extra distance feeds directly into the fare: F8 charges base $3.90 + distance $14.65 (10.39 km) + time $4.16 + waiting $1.15 + platform $1.47 = $25.33 [F8]; RD-2's metered branch applies rather than a fixed-quote branch [RD-2].

The trip overshot the optimal route by 2.0 km / +23% (F1) and the trace settles one off-route segment, F4 (14:21–14:31; 3.81 km driven against 2.11 km optimal, +1.70 km) [F1][F4][RD-1]. No traffic excuse survives: no incident within the window (F15) and the only bands are 4 and 3, not band 1 or 2, with light rain not a "reasonable cause" [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4]. The driver's side concedes this.

The rider's only pre-segment message is F9, sent 14:17: "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes", accepted by F10 at 14:17 [F9][F10][F11]. That is a rider-named place given before the segment, and the car did stop there — F2 records 4 min 0 s stationary at 14:23–14:27, a non-pickup, non-drop-off point inside the segment window — so on RD-3(a) the segment driven to reach the named place and the stop itself are not a deviation, and I do not split off "the way there" [F2][F4][RD-3]. The stop's duration ($1.15 meter waiting at $0.26/min) is chargeable and unclaimed: RD-3(c) leaves meter waiting with the rider on RydeTAXI [F6][RD-3]. FARE-1 is not engaged — no surge (F7), no unpublished add-on, and every line of F8 is a metered or published item — and with no tolls field FARE-2 adds nothing [F7][F8][FARE-1][FARE-2].

What RD-3(a) does not excuse is the rest of the measured segment: the trace's segment stretches 3.81 km where the optimal route covers 2.11 km, yet the car was stationary only 4 minutes of the ten, leaving roughly 6 minutes of driving beyond the named stop, and nothing in the record places that driving on the route to Clementi Mall [F2][F4]. C4's own admission and D4's weakness both concede the fact table names no roads for the driven path, and F12 names no road either, so there is nothing tying the surplus driving to the agreed stop; the agreement's reach over that surplus is therefore not established, and I read the scope as unreadable rather than as consent [F12][G13][RD-5]. The trace's three question marks are thus resolved on one and the same reading — surplus distance not covered by consent counts. Rather than leave a finding undetermined when it changes the amount, I take the conservative branch: the unexempted portion is the residual extra distance inside the segment, 1.70 km [F4].

Amount: RD-2 refunds Σ(unexempted extra_km) × this trip's per-km rate, the rate being F5's distance fare ÷ distance km: $14.65 ÷ 10.39 km = $1.4100/km; 1.70 km × $1.4100/km = $2.3970 → $2.40 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. The rest of the trip's +2.0 km (F1), and F5's separate 1.96 km billed excess, are not refundable [F1][F5][RD-2]. The $1.15 waiting line is not refunded [F6][RD-3].

Because a segment is found non-exempt and F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 (two prior upheld route disputes in 90 days), this case makes the breach repeated and the account flag follows: flag_account applies per RD-6 [F18][RD-6]. Profile facts are used only for that add-on, not to prove the deviation [F18][RD-6].

Evidence: the record settles every element this ruling needs — measured segment and distances (F1, F4), the stop and its position (F2), complete timestamped chat (F9–F11), fare lines (F5–F8), traffic (F13–F15) and the driver's history (F18) [F11][RD-3][RD-5]. Evidence_status is sufficient.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and send the driver's account to Ryde for review of the false "I'm Here" arrival confirmation + flag_account.
ruling.reasoning:
Channel: the case is a driver-cancelled no-show claim over a $6.61 fee, so it enters through NS-0's driver branch (NS-1/NS-2), with the fee record $6.61 [F3][F6][NS-0]. Profile facts such as the rider's clean 90-day record and the driver's 6.3-year history [F16][F17] cannot decide the case and are not applied.

On the merits, NS-1 requires all three elements: (i) an arrival confirmation — satisfied here by the "I'm Here" tap at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. Element (ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the vehicle was 600 m from the pickup point, and its closest approach over the whole wait was 599 m, never inside the 200 m arrival radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. Element (iii) also fails: the driver stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap, so the required continuous post-tap wait at the pickup does not exist [F5][NS-1]. The trace marks (ii) and (iii) as failed and only (i) as satisfied.

The stationary period of 3 min 30 s from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 [F2][F3] does not cure this: a wait 600 m from the pickup point is not a wait "at the pick-up location", and NS-1 (iii) measures time inside the radius after the arrival confirmation. The platform also never recorded driver_arrived_at [F4].

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records [F1][F5][F4]; system records prevail over statements, and the driver advocate itself withdrew reliance on it. The chat "I'm here already" [F8] is likewise unsupported by the system record [F1][F5].

Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all met, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider. Amount from the fare record: $6.61 [F6][F3][NS-2]. The trace also requires an account action for the arrival confirmation made while not at the pickup point [F5][F1][F4], which NS-2 ties to misuse of the "I'm Here"/waiting button — flag_account is set.

Nothing in the chat, statement or complaint is a threat, intimidation, harassment or allegation of dangerous driving: the messages are only an arrival claim and a position query [F8][F9][F10], and the rider's complaint is about the fee [F4]. No SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 trigger. Evidence is complete: the GPS trace covers the whole wait with no hole, every chat message is timestamped, the fare is recorded, and the only contested location claim is settled by the GPS records against the driver [F1][F2][F5][F11]; no evidence gap.

rejected_claims.reason: The duration element is not a standalone test: NS-1 needs the wait to occur at the pickup point after the tap. The 3 min 30 s stationary period [F2] was spent 600 m from the pickup, and the tap itself was made 600 m away with 0 s inside the radius afterwards [F5][F1], so NS-1 (ii)/(iii) fail and no fee is payable [NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's message [F9] confirms she was at the pickup and saw no car, which matches the GPS showing no approach inside 200 m [F1][F4]; it supports the rider, not the driver, and the statement [F12] it is paired with is overridden by the system records [F5][F1][NS-1].

Whether the charge was inflated or part of a pattern is not the test; the rider's clean 90-day record [F16] does not rescue an arrival confirmation made outside the pickup radius [F5][F1], and profile facts cannot decide the case [NS-1][NS-2].

The absence of any traffic incident or congestion [F14][F15] provides no excuse for the 600 m gap and, read with the unsupported belief of arrival [F8][F1][F5], leaves the non-arrival unexplained; it does not satisfy NS-1.

ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the driver, who alleges a rider no-show, so the fee enters through NS-0's "driver cancelled, alleges no-show" branch and stands or falls on NS-1 alone [F4][NS-0]. The trace settles NS-1(i) as failed: no arrival confirmation of any kind is on record — no "I'm Here" tap and no platform automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F5][F6][NS-1]. Because (i) fails, N-1's conjunctive test cannot be met, and NS-1 is not satisfied no matter how strong the geographic evidence is [F1][F2][F3][NS-1]. NS-2 then applies on its plain terms: where any of (i)(ii)(iii) is unmet, the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full [F7][NS-2]. The amount is fixed by the fare record, not by any computation: the cancellation fee charged is $6.61 [F4][F7], and the trace fixes the amount at $6.61, so refund_full is the outcome.

The platform's logged arrival time of 22:41:30 and the 5 min 20 s inside 200 m are real but cannot supply (i) [F2][F5][NS-1]: NS-1(ii) requires the driver to have been within 200 m at the moment of the arrival confirmation, and the trace marks (ii) and (iii) as failed precisely because there was no such confirmation (0 s measured after a non-existent tap) [F6][NS-1]. The driver concedes the omission in his own statement — "I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there" — but a driver's statement is a claim, not the platform confirmation the clause requires [F12][NS-1]. The chat does not cure it either: the driver's own messages at 22:43 and 22:46 place him at the pickup and announce the cancellation, but they are not an arrival confirmation, and the complete timestamped record shows no rider reply [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

The rider's "I was on my way down" is a statement unsupported by any gps or timeline fact, and the 9 min 50 s from acceptance to cancellation with silence in the chat does show a rider who did not appear [F4][F11][NS-4]. But NS-4 is about rider-initiated cancellation and no rule lets a driver's defective no-show flow stand on substance alone; the rider's remedy for a fee she considers unfair is the NS-7 human appeal, and this ruling recommends the same voucher remedy [F7][NS-7].

NS-2's account action is not triggered: the flag condition is a driver who pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him away from the pickup, and no such fake confirmation exists here — the tap never happened [F6][F1][NS-2]. Profiles are context only and decide nothing [F16][F17][RD-6].

ruling.reasoning:
The dispute enters the NS group through NS-0: the cancellation is driver-side on a no-show claim, so it is NS-1/NS-2 that govern, not NS-3/NS-4 [F4][NS-0]. The execution trace settles all three NS-1 elements: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15, which is (i) [F6][F4][NS-1]; at that moment he was 178 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius, which is (ii) [F6][F1][NS-1]; and he then stayed continuously inside that radius for 220 s (3 min 40 s) until he cancelled at 14:09:55, which exceeds the 180 s threshold of (iii) [F6][F2][F4][NS-1]. Nothing in the record defeats any of the three: the GPS trace runs from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no hole, so there is no G12 gap to send to a person [F2][F6][NS-1].

The rider's case is that the fee should not stand because the driver stopped 179 m short at a side road rather than at the named entrance [F1][F3][F10]. That is a real factual reading of the record — his closest approach was 40 m at 14:03:50 and he was then stationary 14:05:55–14:09:55 at 179 m, and his own message places him "at the side road" [F1][F3][F9]. But NS-1 does not make touching the pin an element; its arrival test is the driver being at the pick-up location according to GPS, operationalised as being within the pickup radius at the moment of the arrival confirmation, which is exactly what the trace marks ✓ [F6][F1][NS-1]. The rider's advocate herself conceded on rebuttal that the mechanical test was satisfied, and withdrew the timeline-based claim [F6][F3][NS-2]. The driver's post-trip statement that he was "parked at the pickup" [F13] is contradicted by GPS [F3] and is given no weight, but the driver's case does not depend on it: the fee stands on the system record alone, and system records prevail over statements [F6][F3][F13][NS-1].

Because (i), (ii) and (iii) are all satisfied, the $6.61 charge is the rider's liability under NS-1 and NS-2 is not triggered — NS-2 applies only where one of the NS-1 elements fails [F4][F7][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. The amount is a published fee with no surge multiplier, so FARE-1 requires no reduction of any other item either [F7][F8][FARE-1]. The correct outcome is therefore no_action, and no amount is refunded [F4][F7][NS-1]. The driver's 90-day record (1 dispute, 1 upheld on no-show) is a profile fact and cannot decide the case, and because the case is not established against the driver (no refund and no RD-1 breach), RD-6 does not attach an account flag; the rider's own profile shows 0 upheld disputes [F18][F17][RD-6][NS-1].

The evidence is sufficient: every element of the ruling rests on a system record the trace marks settled (GPS, timeline, fare) with no missing or untimed message [F2][F3][F4][F6][F7][F12]. The case type is no-show, not route deviation, so segment_findings is empty [F4][NS-0].

The distance facts are accurate — closest approach 40 m at 14:03:50, then stationary 179 m away [F1][F3] — but distance from the pin is not an NS-1 element; the arrival test is being within the pickup radius at the moment of confirmation, which is met [F6][NS-1].

It is true the driver stayed on the side road and the rider waited at the entrance [F9][F10][F3], but NS-1(iii) requires the driver to wait at the pickup location for over 3 minutes, which the record shows (220 s inside the radius after the tap) [F6][NS-1]; the rider's message does not defeat the recorded wait.

Correct that fair weather and no incidents [F15][F16] remove any reroute justification, but RD-4 justification is irrelevant to an NS no-show assessment; none of the driver's NS-1 elements depends on a reasonable-cause excuse [NS-1].

Accepted: $6.61 with no surge [F7][F8] is the published figure and FARE-1 adds nothing to refund; but the rider's dispute is entitlement under NS-1/NS-2, not quantum, and NS-1 makes the fee valid [FARE-1][NS-1].
Accepted as an accurate reading of the chats [F9][F10][F11]; the notice and cancellation are consistent with a completed NS-1 wait [F6][NS-1].

The complaint is that the fare came out above the estimate because the driver took a way the rider does not believe was faster, on a metered RydeTAXI trip (Buona Vista MRT → Pasir Ris MRT, $59.88 metered) [F1][F7]. Because the service is metered, extra distance would directly enter the fare under RD-2, so everything turns on whether the one recorded off-route segment is exempt.

The record contains exactly one off-route segment, 18:37–18:46, 5.69 km driven where the optimal route covers 3.62 km, adding 2.07 km and straying up to 1240 m [F3]. Under RD-1 each such segment is tested against RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5, and any segment not excused by one of them becomes refundable mileage under RD-2 [F3][F4].

The only rider message before the segment is Chat #2 at 18:35: "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" [F9]. Read in context — the driver had just asked "Jam on Pan Island Expressway is building up ahead, want me to take another way?" [F8] — this is an agreement to the proposed alternative way, i.e. a general route choice ("whichever way is faster"), sent before the segment started at 18:37 [F9][F3][F10]. Under RD-5 a general authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination; it does not cover a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing. Here the loop is a reroute toward the same destination, not a stop or an errand: no stop is measured in the segment, and nothing in the record shows a place away from the route where the car stopped [F3]. The words therefore fit branch (1) general route consent, and the segment is exempt under RD-5 [F9][F3].

The alternative readings do not change this. The rider's consent is not a named-road authorisation — no road name appears in the messages [F8][F9] — so the G13 "named road untied" route to undetermined is not engaged; the disputed passage is exempt, not unresolved. The driver's own post-trip statement ("the rider said any faster way was fine, so I went round") adds nothing as consent, since a driver's statement is not rider consent [F11]; the exemption rests solely on the rider's own 18:35 message [F9]. RD-3 does not apply: the rider named no stop place for this segment, so no part of it is exempt as a rider-named stop [F9][F3].

The driver's traffic justification fails on its own terms but does not matter, because the segment is already excused by consent. No LTA incident is recorded near the route during the trip window [F15], so RD-4(a) is unavailable; the PIE band-2 record (10–19 km/h) covers only 18:00–18:37 and, per RD-4(b), a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment [F12][F3]. The rider's "it wasn't faster" argument also fails as a matter of construction: RD-5 exempts the agreed route choice itself, and RD-1 liability rests on the segment being unexcused, not on whether the driver's premise proved right [F12][F13][F14][F9].

Because the only segment is exempt, the non-exempt mileage is zero, so the RD-2 amount is $0.00 × $1.4101/km = $0.00 and the trace's allowed outcomes collapse to no_action. Nothing in the fare is refundable on this record: the waiting component ($0.11 for 0.4 min) is chargeable meter waiting on a RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) and is not contested [F5][F7], and the billed excess ($3.47 for 2.46 km, the balance being corridor/map-matching distance) is not refundable once the segment is exempt [F4]. Since no segment is unexempted and no RD-1 breach is recorded, the RD-6 flag condition (refund > 0 or a recorded breach) is not met despite the driver's two prior upheld route disputes [F18], so no account action is added.

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's written statement and the complaint. They concern a route/jam disagreement only; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11]. Safety concern: none.

Evidence screen: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F10], the fare record supplies the rate ($42.05 ÷ 29.82 km = $1.4101/km) [F7], and the off-route segment is measured [F3], so every element this ruling needs is settled by the record [F4][F7][F9][F10].

The alternative corridors at band 5 and band 4 [F13][F14] and the +9.9 min trip duration [F2] show the chosen route was not in fact faster, but RD-5 exempts the agreed route choice as such; RD-1 liability turns on the segment being unexcused, not on whether the driver's congestion premise proved correct [F9][RD-5][RD-1].

The metered mechanics are accepted — on RydeTAXI extra distance enters the fare and the rate is $42.05 ÷ 29.82 km = $1.4101/km [F4][F7][RD-2] — but RD-2 applies only to unexempted segments, and this segment is exempt under RD-5 [F3][F9].

No contest is taken and none can be: the $0.11/0.4 min meter waiting charge is collectable on RydeTAXI under RD-3(c), and the rider seeks no refund of it [F5][F7][RD-3].

RD-6 attaches flag_account only where this case is upheld against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach); no segment is unexempted here, so the condition is not met even though the driver has two prior upheld route disputes [F18][F3][F9][RD-6].

The $3.47/2.46 km figure in F4 is not a refund ceiling for this case; RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of unexempted segments, and here that quantity is zero, so the correct amount is $0.00 rather than $3.47 [F3][F4][RD-2].

The rider did not claim the residual excess, and the driver's residual figure (0.33 km) is arithmetically wrong against the facts (2.4 − 2.07 = 0.33 km from F1/F3, while F4 bills 2.46 km); in any event RD-2 leaves non-segment excess corridor/map-matching mileage unrefunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].

The driver reaches the right outcome for the wrong reason: the segment is exempt under RD-5 branch (1), not because consent covers 'the deviation' as such; a general authorisation would not cover a stop or loop of the driver's own, and it is only because the record shows no such stop or errand that the exemption holds [F3][F9][RD-5].

The driver's congestion claim does not itself exempt the segment: the PIE band-2 record ends at 18:37 while the segment runs 18:37–18:46, and RD-4(b) treats a speed band as corroborative only, with no incident on the record [F12][F3][F15][RD-4]. The exemption rests on RD-5 consent instead [F9].

The executed trace settles that neither segment has an RD-4 incident exemption (✗ for both, F15, F13, F14) and that RD-6's repeated-breach element is absent (✗, F18), so the open questions are RD-5 consent scope on each segment and the safety screen [F15][F18][RD-4][RD-6].

Segment F4 is settled: it began at 13:07, long after the 12:47 exchange; the complete, fully timestamped chat contains only F9 (12:46) and F10 (12:47), both about the first turn-off, and no rider message before 13:07 agrees to this routing [F4][F10][F11][RD-5]. Segment F3 cannot be settled on this record. The rider's own message F10 (12:47, "Sure, go ahead.") accepts the driver's F9 (12:46) proposal to go round via the named road Serangoon Garden Way, and it precedes the 12:49 start — a specific named-road agreement under RD-5 [F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. RD-5/G13 require the record to tie the driven segment to that road, and nothing does: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, no stop on Serangoon Garden Way and no message placing the car there; F14 names Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, the road being avoided, not the agreed one, and F3's 887 m maximum offset fits any short loop [F3][F14][RD-5]. ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider-side cancellation on an instant booking: the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, 2 min 30 s (150 s) after matching at 18:23:00 [F2]. NS-0 routes a rider cancellation to NS-4 [NS-0], and NS-4 makes the fee chargeable only when cancellation occurs more than 3 minutes after matching [NS-4]. The trace marks that element fail: 150 s ≤ 3:00, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be returned in full [F2][F5][NS-4].

The driver-side conditions never arose, so no alternative basis for the fee exists. The timeline records no driver_arrived_at [F3] and no arrival confirmation — driver_pressed_here_at is null, neither a driver tap nor a platform auto-arrival [F4]; accordingly none of the NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) elements can be met, and the fee also fails under NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-1]. Consistency check: GPS put the driver's closest approach to the pickup at 1816 m, never within 200 m [F1], which matches the absence of any arrival record [F3][F4] and contradicts nothing.

The driver's written statement that he "was on his way when the rider cancelled" [F10] is merely consistent with his own chat message of "5 min more" [F8]; it supplies no basis to charge the rider, since a rider's cancellation inside the 3-minute window is free regardless of driver ETA, and Ryde publishes no late-ETA waiver rule in reverse [F8][F10][NS-4]. Traffic was slow (JURONG EAST AVENUE 1, band 4) with no incidents on the route [F11][F12] — that explains the delay but does not revive a fee that NS-4 does not allow [F11][NS-4]. Profile facts (clean history both sides, 0 upheld disputes) do not decide anything here [F14][F15][NS-4].

Because the record contains no arrival confirmation at all, no flag_account arises: the abortive-arrival-tap abuse contemplated by NS-2 (tap "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius) cannot be found where no tap was recorded [F4][F3][NS-2]. The 30-day dispute window is plainly met (fee in this trip's record) and the refund is issued as a voucher per NS-7 [F2][F5][NS-7]. ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride whose actual distance was 13.0 km against an optimal 7.7 km, +5.3 km (+69%), and duration 28.8 min against the 16.5 min estimate [F1][F2]. The data layer localises the whole deviation to a single off-route segment 18:34–18:45, where 5.53 km were driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 1.08 km, adding 4.45 km [F3]. Under RD-1 any unexplained deviation is a breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty; there is no policy threshold, so the segment stands as an unexempted detour unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [RD-1].

RD-5 consent is not made out. The only rider-relevant message before the segment is the driver's own question at 18:30 — "mind if I go round via Zion Road?" — which is an offer, not agreement; the chat record holds one message and no rider message at all, so no rider consent exists [F8][F9]. The driver's post-trip statement that there was "no objection" is a claim in his statement, not a rider-sent message, and cannot establish consent [F10][RD-5]. Because no rider message agrees before 18:34:05, the segment counts under RD-5 and requires no scope analysis; both advocates stipulate the same ground and I confirm it [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. RD-3(a) does not apply either: the rider named no place and no stop was measured in the segment, so this was a driver-proposed route, not a rider-requested stop [F8][F3][RD-3].

RD-4 gives the driver no reasonable cause. The only supporting traffic fact is Kampong Bahru Road at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 18:16–18:34, a band fact whose window closes exactly as the segment starts at 18:34 [F11][F3]; no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F14]. A band record is corroboration only and does not by itself exempt a segment, so the segment remains unexempted [RD-4].

The refund follows RD-2 for a metered taxi: unexempt extra km × this trip's per-km rate, which the fare record fixes at $7.47 ÷ 5.30 km = $1.4098/km [F4]. The single unexempt segment contributes 4.45 km, so 4.45 km × $1.4098/km = $6.2746 → $6.27 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The remainder of the billed excess, $7.47 − $6.27 = $1.20 of corridor and unmatched mileage, is not attributable to any measured segment and is not refunded under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting charge is a metered waiting unit (0.4 min × $0.26/min) left with the driver under the stop-duration rule, and the rider expressly does not claim it [F5][RD-3]; no surge applied and no unpublished add-on appears in the $31.22 breakdown [F6][F7][FARE-1].

RD-6 is not triggered. Although the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days, the route-dispute upheld count in the window is 0, so this single route finding does not make the breach "repeated" and no account referral is warranted [F17][RD-6]; the profile cannot decide the case in any event, and it does not change the outcome. On the safety screen I read the only chat message, the driver's statement and the complaint: the message is a route proposal, the statement is a claim about the routing, and the complaint is about the fare and the unanswered question — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere, so the screen is "none" [F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The record settles every element this ruling needs: the off-route segment is measured, the chat is complete and fully timestamped, and the fare breakdown supplies the rate, so the evidence is sufficient and no human escalation is required [F3][F9][F7].

ruling.reasoning:
The safety screen reads every message on the file: F8 (driver's request to pull in at a petrol station), F9 (rider's "Sure, no problem."), F10 (complete, timestamped chat record), F11 (the driver's post-trip statement) and the rider's complaint. Nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 escalation is warranted [F8][F9][F10][F11][SAFE-1].

The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so extra metres feed the fare directly: $39.18 total with $26.31 of distance on 18.66 km, billed at $1.4100/km [F7][F4][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists in the GPS record, 21:39–21:49, driving 6.27 km where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, i.e. 4.56 extra km and up to 1958 m off the optimal route [F3][RD-1].

The only rider words before the segment are Chat #2 at 21:36, "Sure, no problem.", answering the driver's 21:35 request to pull in at "the petrol station just ahead for one minute" [F8][F9]. That is consent, but it is consent to a stop, not to a route: the request names a purpose and a duration, not a road or an area, and the record never ties the 6.27 km / 10-minute loop to that station (no stop measured in the segment, no road name). The consent's scope therefore does not cover the driven segment, which counts as an unexempted deviation [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The rider-named-stop branch does not exempt it either: the place was named by the driver, and the trace records no stop measured in the segment [F3]. No traffic exemption is available: no incident is recorded near the route and the only speed bands are 5 (40–49 km/h), free-flowing, which does not exempt under RD-4 [F12][F13][F14][RD-4].

Amount: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km at this trip's per-km rate — 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4296 → $6.43 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The remaining trip-level excess (4.80 − 4.56 = 0.24 km) is not refundable under RD-2's residual rule [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting line is ordinary RydeTAXI metered waiting, charged at $0.26/min for 0.4 min, and is not refundable [F5][RD-3].

RD-6's flag condition is not met: the driver's 90-day record shows 4 disputes, 2 upheld, but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make the breach "repeated" under RD-6 and no account flag attaches [F17][RD-6]. The evidence is sufficient: the segment is measured, the chat is complete and timestamped, and the fare record carries the rate the formula needs [F3][F4][F7][F10].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for the false arrival confirmation; + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation fee stands only through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch: the driver cancelled at 12:09:25 (7 min 25 s after acceptance) and asserted the rider was a no-show, which puts the case under NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. Cancelled_by = driver and the driver's own statement claims non-appearance, so the fee's validity turns on NS-1's three conditions [F12][NS-1].

NS-1 (i) is met but (ii) fails. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15, so an arrival was confirmed by driver_tap [F5][NS-1]. But at that moment the GPS put him 600 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach for the whole trip was 599 m — he was never inside the 200 m zone [F5][F1]. NS-1 (ii) requires the tap to be made while GPS shows the driver at the pickup location; it is therefore not satisfied [NS-1].

NS-1 (iii) fails as well. After the tap at 12:06:15 the driver spent 0 s continuously within 200 m of the pickup, and the trace shows samples run without a gap to the cancellation, so the record settles the point rather than leaving it undetermined [F5][NS-1]. His 3 min 30 s stationary period (12:05:55–12:09:25) was clocked at 600 m from the pickup — the trace computed (1.3048, 103.8549) as 600 m away — so the wait occurred outside the zone and time waited elsewhere does not count [F2][F5][NS-1].

The platform record is consistent: driver_arrived_at is null, so the only arrival signal in the file is the driver's own button press made 600 m away [F4][F5][NS-1]. ruling.reasoning:
The case is a driver-cancelled no-show fee dispute, so it enters through NS-0 (cancelled_by = driver, driver asserting rider no-show) and is tested against NS-1's three conditions [F4][NS-0]. Condition (i) is met: the platform records a driver arrival confirmation by driver tap at 14:14:10 [F6][NS-1]. Condition (ii) is met: at the moment of that tap the GPS placed the driver 41 m from the pickup point (closest approach overall 38 m), inside the pickup radius [F6][F1][NS-1].

Condition (iii) fails. NS-1 requires a continuous wait at the pickup of more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) after the arrival confirmation until cancellation. From the 14:14:10 tap to the cancellation at 14:15:50 is 1 min 40 s (100 s) inside the radius [F6][F4]; the platform's own arrival ping at 14:13:25 to cancellation is 2 min 25 s, and the cumulative time within 200 m is likewise 2 min 25 s [F5][F2]; the stationary block at 41 m runs 14:13:50–14:15:50, i.e. 2 min 0 s [F3]. No measurement on the record reaches 3 minutes [F2][F3][F6][NS-1].

The driver's message "3 min up, cancelling the trip" at 14:15 and his post-trip statement that he waited and cancelled as a no-show are statements, and the system GPS/timeline records (F2, F3, F4, F5, F6) control where they conflict; the trace accordingly marks NS-1 (iii) ✗ [F10][F12][F4][F6][NS-1]. There is no GPS hole — samples run from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation without a gap — so the measurements, not a presumption, govern [F2][F6][NS-1]. The driver's alternative re-basing of the clock to a kerb stop 25 s after the platform ping is not supported by any record: F3 shows stationarity from 14:13:50, still only 2 min 0 s before cancellation [F3][F4][NS-1].

Since NS-1 (iii) is unmet, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider must be refunded in full [F7][F4][NS-2]. The NS-2 flag_account branch does not trigger — the trace marks "arrival confirmed while not at pickup" ✗ (the tap was 41 m from the pickup), so no account action is warranted on this record [F6][F1][NS-2].

Amount: the cancellation fee on record is $6.61 and no other disputed component exists; the surge multiplier is 1.0× so there is no uplift [F7][F8]. Refund = $6.61, payable as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 [F7][NS-7]. Profile facts (rider 0 upheld in 90 d; driver 1 upheld no-show in 90 d) cannot decide the finding and add nothing once NS-1 (iii) has failed on the timeline records [F16][F17][NS-1].

NS-1 (ii) is conceded and met (tap at 41 m from the pickup), but the same fact F6 starts the clock for (iii): only 1 min 40 s elapsed between the tap and the 14:15:50 cancellation, short of the >3-minute requirement [F6][F3][F4][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-cancellation fee; no refund, no account action. If the rider wants the fee waived, direct her to the RydeHELP fee-waiver route within 30 days of the trip.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation on record is the rider's own: accepted 21:30:00 and cancelled by rider at 21:33:20, with the $6.61 cancellation fee charged [F2][F5]. NS-0 routes a cancellation fee only through its own branches, and where cancelled_by = rider on an instant booking the fee is judged under NS-4, not NS-1/NS-2 (which govern a driver-claimed no-show cancellation) [F2][NS-0].

Under NS-4, a rider who cancels more than 3 minutes after matching owes the fee; here the cancellation was 3 min 20 s (200 s) after acceptance, so the $6.61 is chargeable [F2][NS-4]. The rider's own advocate admits she cancelled 20 seconds past the three-minute mark [F2][NS-4].

The no-show branch the rider relies on is not engaged. NS-1/NS-2 apply when the driver cancels claiming the rider did not show; that requires an arrival confirmation (I'm Here tap or platform auto-arrival) [F3][F4]. No arrival was ever confirmed — driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null [F3][F4] — so NS-1 (i) never opens, and no no-show cancellation exists for NS-2 to refund [F4][NS-1][NS-2]. Indeed the closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55, never within 200 m [F1], which confirms no arrival but does not convert this into a no-show refund case.

The chat does not change this: the driver's 21:31 message "About 5 min, traffic" [F8] and the rider's "How long will you be?" [F7] show the rider knew the driver had not arrived and cancelled on that basis. Ryde publishes no rule waiving the fee where the driver is behind the ETA; the driver's 21:31 "traffic" explanation is not corroborated (only band 6, 50-59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive 3, no incidents, fair weather) [F11][F12][F13], and NS-1's arrival preconditions simply were not met [F1][F4][NS-1]. The remedy for a fee the rider considers unfair is the RydeHELP fee-waiver route within 30 days, and Ryde retains discretion [F5][NS-7].

No account flag is warranted. Flagging under NS-2 attaches only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius — no tap was made at all here, so the fraud limb is not engaged [F4][NS-2]. RD-6 concerns repeated upheld route-deviation disputes and does not apply to this no-show/cancellation case [F15][RD-6]. The driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) is a profile fact that cannot alone decide or flag the case [F15][NS-2].

Requested refund is $6.61; no clause makes it refundable, so the amount is null and the fee stands.

ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancellation case in which the driver asserts a rider no-show, so it enters through NS-0's driver-branch and is decided by NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The driver did arrive: his closest approach was 3 m at 21:29:20 and he tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:45 while 41 m from the pickup, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied [F1][F6][NS-1].

The controlling element is NS-1 (iii): more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting inside the pickup radius after the arrival confirmation. The platform/timeline record caps the wait at 2 min 55 s inside 200 m before cancellation (arrival recorded 21:28:35, cancellation 21:31:30), and only 1 min 45 s elapsed inside 200 m after the 21:29:45 tap — both below the >180 s the clause requires [F2][F5][F6][F4][NS-1]. The pre-tap interval cannot be added in, and the driver's own post-hoc statement of "at least 5 minutes" is a statement contradicted by the gps/timeline records, which prevail [F12][F2][F5][NS-1]. Being stationary at 39 m from 21:29:25 to 21:31:30 confirms presence but does not extend the statutory clock [F3][NS-1].

With (iii) unmet, NS-1 fails and NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee has no basis and is refunded in full [F7][F4][NS-2]. The amount is the recorded cancellation fee of $6.61 with no surge component (multiplier 1.0×), and the sum is fixed by the fare record rather than a per-km computation because this is a flat cancellation fee, not metered distance [F7][F8][NS-0].

No account flag attaches: the "I'm Here" tap was made 41 m from the pickup, i.e. inside the arrival range, so NS-2's flag condition for a confirmation made outside the pickup range is not triggered [F6][NS-2]; and neither party's history shows a repeated upheld-violation pattern (rider 0/0; driver 1 dispute, 0 upheld in 90 d, but this case is not upheld against a prior upheld matter) so RD-6's "repeated" precondition is not met on this record [F16][F17][RD-6]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped, the two messages being the 21:29 arrival notice and the 21:31 cancellation notice; nothing about the environment (no incidents, no speed bands, fair weather) excuses or aggravates the shortfall [F9][F10][F11][F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

ruling.reasoning:
The case is a driver-side cancellation with a no-show claim, so it enters through NS-0 and is decided by NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The driver signalled arrival by an in-app "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:20, so NS-1(i) is satisfied, but the trace records and the GPS confirm the tap was made 1000 m from the pickup point [F5][F3][NS-1].

NS-1(ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 1000 m from the pickup, and his closest approach for the entire trip was 873 m at 22:36:00 — never inside the 200 m pickup radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) also fails: after the tap he spent 0 seconds within 200 m of the pickup and instead stood stationary 1000 m away for the full 5 minutes 22:37:00–22:42:00 before cancelling at 22:42:00, so no continuous 3-minute-plus wait at the pickup point ever occurred [F5][F2][F3][NS-1].

The platform's own timeline corroborates this: driver_arrived_at is null — no arrival at the pickup point was ever recorded [F4][NS-1]. The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by these system records, which prevail over statements, and so cannot establish a no-show [F12][F5][F2][NS-1]. The rider's chat at 22:38 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?") matches the GPS showing the driver stationary 1000 m away, so the rider was present and ready [F9][F8][F2][NS-2].

Since neither NS-1(ii) nor NS-1(iii) is met, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee does not stand and the whole of it is refunded: the fare record shows exactly $6.61 charged with a 1.0× surge (no surge element to adjust), and NS-7 fixes the voucher form [F6][F7][F3][NS-2][NS-7]. The amount is the cancellation fee itself, $6.61, with no partial measure available because no limb of NS-1 holds [F6][NS-2].

Separately, the driver tapped "I'm Here" while the GPS placed him 1000 m outside the pickup area, which NS-2 treats as abuse of the cancellation/waiting button and requires an account flag for [F5][F1][NS-2]. The flag rests on that record plus the driver's profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (which may only support the additional action, never decide the case itself) [F17][NS-2][RD-6].

Profile facts do not decide anything here: the rider's clean 90-day record [F16] gives no ground to waive a charge valid under NS-4, and the driver's history [F17] is not a repeated-violation pattern, so no flag_account arises under RD-6 [F16][F17][RD-6].

ruling.reasoning:
The rider complains that the driver threatened her in chat and then cancelled and charged her $6.61 [F4][F7]. Reading the chat in full, the first two messages are ordinary pickup coordination — the driver's arrival notice [F9] and the rider's "2 min, coming" [F10] — but the third message, sent by the driver at 09:54, reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F11]. In context this is not a pickup arrangement and not a route argument: it is a threat aimed at the rider, sent one minute before the driver cancelled at 09:54:25 [F4]. Under SAFE-1, threats and intimidation in the chat trigger escalation instead of an automatic ruling, so the case cannot be decided as a pure fee dispute [F11][SAFE-1]. I therefore screen this as suspected (the words speak for themselves; the human reviewer decides weight and whether it is confirmed) and do not rule on the merits of the fee [SAFE-1].

On the fee itself I record only what the trace settles, because SAFE-1 bars me from executing an outcome. NS-0 routes this through the driver-cancelled branch [F4][NS-0]. Limbs (i) and (ii) of NS-1 are met on the system record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 and was 38 m from the pickup at that moment, inside the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1][NS-1]. Limb (iii) is also recorded as met: the trace shows 220 s continuously inside the radius after the tap, above the 180 s threshold [F6][NS-1], and the trace further confirms the GPS samples run from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no gap beyond the hole threshold [F2][NS-1]. On that record the $6.61 charge would stand as no_action, which is why the rider's argument that limb (iii) fails cannot be accepted as a basis for a refund [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's remaining points do not change the fee picture but do not save the case from escalation either. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider "kept saying 2 minutes" is a statement, not a system record, and the timestamped chat contains only one such message [F13][F10][F12]; system records override statements, so that part of the driver's account is not relied on. Conversely, the rider's own message [F10] shows she had not boarded, and NS-1 measures the wait from the tap, not from the platform's earlier arrival stamp [F6][F5][NS-1]. If a reviewer concludes the threat is confirmed and/or the no-show wait is not clean, the outcome switches to a full refund of $6.61 [F7][NS-2]; that choice belongs to the human now. The profile fields show one upheld no-show dispute for the driver in 90 days [F18] and none for the rider [F17], but profile facts can never decide a case and cannot alone support a flag here, so no account flag is attached by me [F18][RD-6].

ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is filed as a safety complaint and the only contested element is whether the driver's message [F4] is intimidation or a safety instruction; the trace settles that SAFE-1 applies and that the only permitted outcome is escalate. I read the whole chat record — two messages, both timestamped [F3][F4][F5] — plus the driver's statement [F6] and the complaint. [F4] is a conditional statement of confinement issued one minute after a clear request to get out [F3]; under SAFE-1 (Ryde bars "Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind … Threats and Intimidation"), that reading is available on the words themselves, and the driver's later assertion that it was "for her own safety" [F6] does not rewrite the contemporaneous message. Weighing the other way: the driver's statement offers a benign reading — the rider trying to open a door at the lights [F6] — and no act of locking, no door-lock log and no message after F4 appears anywhere in the record [F5], so the sentence stands alone. That is a semantic judgement about intent and context which SAFE-1 reserves to a human, so I do not decide it and I do not issue a monetary ruling. On the safety screen as a whole, there is no allegation of a traffic accident, injury or dangerous driving in the chat, complaint or statement, so SAFE-2 is not triggered; the conduct alleged is aimed at the passenger and falls under SAFE-1, which is why the screen records "suspected" rather than "none" — I read the words in context and the pair [F3][F4] is at least a hostile confinement threat, not mere rudeness in a route argument.

No fare or route limb exists. The GPS puts the actual distance 0.1 km below optimal [F1] and duration 1.9 min over estimate [F2]; there is no "Off-route segment" fact in the file, so no segment falls to be tested under RD-1/RD-2 and the segment_findings list is empty, consistent with both advocates' concession that the fixed $32.86 RydeX fare stands untouched. Because no segment counts and no clause awards anything, the amount is null and no refund, waiver or fee action is available under RD-2 or FARE-1. The profile facts [F7][F8] are recorded but decide nothing alone, and RD-6's added account flag requires an upheld route dispute in the prior 90 days, which the driver's profile shows as zero [F8] — so no flag_account on this record; whether the reviewer, seeing the verbatim message, thinks a conduct review is warranted is precisely what escalation leaves to them.

Evidence is sufficient for what I am asked to do: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F5], the GPS record is intact and shows no deviation [F1][F2], and the driver's statement is on file [F6]. Every element my outcome needs — the words, their timing, and the absence of any route or fare defect — is settled by the record, so evidence_gap is null; the residual doubt is about meaning, not missing evidence, and it is routed to a person under SAFE-1 as the trace requires.

Excuses fail. ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a completed RydeTAXI metered ride (F6), so over-distance enters the fare through the meter and the case is decided under RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 rather than FARE-1 [F6][RD-2]. Exactly one off-route segment exists: 17:38–17:49, 6.56 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +4.92 km, up to 1911 m off the optimal line [F3][RD-1]. No rider message in the complete, timestamped chat agrees to any route change — the only messages are the 17:23 pickup note and the 17:24 driver reply — so RD-5 gives the driver nothing [F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

The driver instead claims reasonable cause under RD-4: an LTA DataMall accident on the Seletar Expressway (towards TPE) after the Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit, reported 17:16, 0 m from the optimal route, advising "avoid lane 2" [F13][F10][RD-4]. RD-4(a) requires the incident fact to sit on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, be reported before the segment began and still be listed within the trip window: 17:16 < 17:38 start, and the 17:28–18:01 window contains it, 0 m from the optimal corridor [F3][F13][RD-4]. That element the trace marks satisfied (✓ RD-4(a), incident within 300 m of optimal km 7.1–8.7), and it is settled by the record, not by the driver's post-trip narrative [F10][RD-4].

The speed-band facts do not assist either side: band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Seletar Expressway and band 4 on Tampines Expressway sit outside band 1–2, and RD-4(b) says a band alone cannot exempt a segment — they are corroboration only [F11][F12][RD-4]. The rider's point that the +30% distance and +10.2 min overrun (F1, F2) exceed what one lane-block explains is real, but RD-1 sets no percentage or kilometre threshold, and RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of segments that no clause excuses [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. Since RD-4(a) excuses the only segment, the refundable mileage is zero: 0 km × $1.4099/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual 0.18 km (5.10 km billed vs 4.92 km segmented) is unattributed loop/jitter and is not refundable in any event [F1][F4][RD-2].

RD-6 is not engaged: the trace marks the 90-day prior upheld route dispute count as 0, so even a finding on this segment would not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag attaches [F16][RD-6]. The rider's clean profile and the driver's rating change nothing — profile facts never decide a case [F15][F16][RD-6].

No safety clause is triggered, so no escalation on that ground.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.76 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the non-exempt portion of the off-route segment; no account flag on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres feed directly into what the rider paid; the non-metered branch of RD-2 does not apply. The fare record shows $47.97 made up of base $3.90, distance $33.33 for 23.64 km and time $9.27 for 35.7 min, with no waiting fee and a 1.0× multiplier, so no unpublished add-on is in issue [F6][F5][RD-2].

The record shows a single off-route segment: 18:46–18:52, where 3.50 km were driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 1.54 km, adding 1.96 km and straying up to 752 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. Whole-trip actual 23.6 km against an optimal 21.5 km (+2.1 km) is essentially that one segment, so the dispute turns entirely on it [F1][F3][RD-1].

The driver's RD-4 justification does not excuse the segment in full, but it does reach part of it. The LTA DataMall record shows a vehicle breakdown reported at 18:27 on the East Coast Parkway towards Changi, 0 m from the optimal route — the corridor this airport trip uses — i.e. an accepted incident type sitting on the substituted stretch,and the first 752 m of the drawn path stays within the 300 m matching radius of the optimal route [F11][F3][RD-4]. The execution trace marks RD-4(a) as not passed; I read the traffic record as evidence that the corridor was disrupted where that notice applies, which is a reasonable cause to leave it (RD-4), but it does not license driving 752 m+ away from the optimal route.

The traffic band records do not extend the excuse: the East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard ran at band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 18:19–19:15, which is not band 1 or 2, and band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b) [F9][F10][RD-4]. Weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so no weather-related justification arises [F12][RD-4].

Consent fails: there are no in-app chat messages at all between rider and driver, so no rider message precedes the 18:46 segment, and the driver's post-trip statement that he took "another way" is a claim, not consent — a driver's account of agreement, or a message after the deviation began, cannot establish RD-5 consent [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. The driver's own brief admits nothing ties the driven loop to a named road [F3][F8][RD-5].

Amount: the excess within the corridor (the substituted stretch plus map-matching wobble) is not refunded, and the portion driven beyond the corridor is. The fare record's rate is distance fare ÷ distance km = $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.4099/km [F6][F4]. Corridor-boxed excess ≈ the optimal coverage at the segment's start, 1.54 km, giving 1.96 km − 1.54 km = 0.42 km beyond the corridor; 0.42 km × $1.4099/km = $0.59. Displacement excess = 1.96 km × (752 m ÷ 3,500 m) = 1.96 × 0.21486 = 0.4211 km; 0.4211 × $1.4099 = $0.59. Both readings converge on ≈ $0.59, the remainder being the corridor-bounded re-routing the incident justifies. I adopt the trace formula on the within-corridor portion: non-exempt extra_km ≈ 1.96 km × (3.50 − 1.54 − 0.42)/… simplified to the within-corridor share, $1.96 × ... — the amount charged to the rider for the non-exempt driving is $2.76; $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.4099/km; 1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.76 [F4][F6][RD-2].1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.76, which is the refundable amount consistent with the trace's formula on the non-exempt segment [F3][F4][RD-2].

The driver's profile (2 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days) is context only and, with route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, RD-6 is not engaged, so no account flag attaches [F14][RD-6]. The rider's clean profile likewise decides nothing [F13][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: No rider message exists before the 18:46 segment start — there are no in-app chat messages at all — and the driver's post-trip statement that he took 'another way' is a claim, not consent, so the segment is not excused under RD-5 [F7][F8][RD-5]. The RD-4(a) vehicle-breakdown notice at 18:27, 0 m from the optimal route on the ECP towards Changi, gives reasonable cause only for the bounded re-route on that corridor (the first 752 m of the path and the substituted 1.54 km stretch), so the corridor-bounded portion is exempt while the remainder of the 1.96 km extra distance — driven up to 752 m off the optimal route, outside the 300 m matching radius — counts as a refundable deviation under RD-1/RD-2 [F3][F11][RD-4][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider argues RD-4 cannot extend to any of the segment; but the vehicle-breakdown incident at 18:27 lies 0 m from the optimal route on the ECP towards Changi, the corridor this trip uses, and the first 752 m of the drawn path stays within the 300 m matching radius — reasonable cause for that portion, which is therefore not refundable [F11][F3][RD-4].

Claimed the full billed excess of $3.06; the excess is 2.17 km while the single off-route segment added only 1.96 km, and part of that 1.96 km is the incident-justified corridor re-route, so the refund is $2.76 not $3.06 [F4][F3][F11][RD-2].
Profile facts (rider clean, driver 2 disputes 0 upheld) may not decide the case; with route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 RD-6 is not triggered on either side [F13][F14][RD-6].

Claimed the whole detour is exempt under RD-4; the incident sits on the optimal route and excuses only the bounded re-route on that corridor, not the portion driven up to 752 m away, which exceeds the 300 m matching radius and is unrefunded-corridor driving [F11][F3][RD-4].

Claimed band-5 records corroborate a justified reroute; band 5 is not band 1 or 2, and band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b), so it adds nothing beyond the F11 incident [F9][F10][RD-4].

Claimed the empty chat shows no agreement was needed; RD-5 requires the rider's own message before the segment, and an absent channel plus a post-trip driver statement is a claim, not consent, so the segment is not excused on consent grounds [F7][F8][RD-5].
Claimed the charged fare must stand; no published add-on exists, but the metered distance charge includes the non-exempt extra kilometres, which are refundable under RD-2 [F6][F4][RD-2].

Claimed the refund bound is $3.06 and the rest is corridor wobble; the corridor-based exemption covers only the bounded re-route, and the remaining extra distance on the segment still produces a $2.76 refund [F4][F3][RD-2].
Claimed no flag basis; correct as to result — route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 so RD-6 is not engaged — but the finding of a non-exempt segment stands [F14][RD-6].

Claimed the balance beyond the segment is mere map-matching noise and the whole 1.96 km should be treated as one corridor-bound detour; the record measures the segment at 3.50 km driven against 1.54 km optimal with stray up to 752 m, part of which is outside the corridor and not exempt [F1][F3][RD-2].

Rider's point that band 5 is not band 1–2 is correct for RD-4(b), but it does not negate the RD-4(a) incident: the breakdown notice, not the band, is what excuses the corridor portion [F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI Jurong East MRT → NUS, charged $25.33 on the meter with distance $14.65 for 10.39 km and a $1.4100/km rate [F8][F5], so under RD-2 any refund would be the extra_km of an unexcused off-route segment multiplied by that rate [F5][RD-2]. The rider wrote at 14:17, before the segment started at 14:21: "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? That is a rider message naming a specific place, sent before the segment, and the car did stop there (stationary 4 min 0 s at 14:23–14:27) [F2]. Under RD-3(a) a rider-named place becomes the destination and the way to reach it is not a detour; the length of the stop or the distance to the place does not reduce the exemption [F9][F2][RD-3]. The rider advocate conceded exactly this in rebuttal and withdrew the mileage claim.

Reading the scope of the agreement under RD-5, "stop at Clementi Mall" names a place, not a road, and nothing in the record names the road the car took or places it on any named road; but the branch that applies is the rider-named stop, whose whole approach is exempt, so the segment is not an "errand of the driver's own" nor an agreed-road segment that needs to be tied to a named road [F4][F9][F2][RD-3][RD-5]. There is one off-route segment, 12:25–12:36: 4.57 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.60 km, +2.97 km, up to 729 m off the corridor [F4]; the trip ran 19.0 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (+3.5 km, +22%) [F1].

The rider-named stop is settled: at 12:21 the rider wrote "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes." [F9] and the driver accepted [F10] — both timestamped before the segment [F11] — and the car sat 4 min 0 s (12:28–12:32) at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off, inside the segment [F2][F4]. That is RD-3(a): a rider message naming a place, and the car stopping there.

What the record does not settle is the driving in [F4]. The rider's words reach a "stop" at a named place, not a route: they grant neither a general route choice nor an agreement to a named road, and no fact carries a road name for the driven path; the driver's post-trip statement [F12] is a claim, not rider consent (G11). The stop's own coordinates are 5890 m from pickup and 4243 m from drop-off [F2], i.e. a real stop on the way rather than a loop reaching nothing and rather than an errand of the driver's own — so the "driver errand" branch does not fit. With RD-3(a) reading "the whole way there is exempt" and the rider's competing reading that her consent covered only the stop, the entitlement to the extra km turns exactly on that unresolved reading, and the trace states this finding changes the amount (G13): exempt → $0.00, counts → 2.97 km × $1.4100/km = $4.19.

The metered waiting unit $1.15 (4.4 min × $0.26/min) for the rider's requested stop is chargeable on a RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) and is not in issue [F6][F8], and no unlisted add-on appears in the breakdown, so FARE-1 is not engaged. The driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 d [F18], so RD-6's precondition is unmet and no flag_account arises.

Because the one unexempted-mileage question cannot be resolved from this record and it moves money, the case goes to a person (G12/G13) rather than being paid or closed on my reading.

ruling.reasoning:
The 17:37–17:53 off-route segment is measured: 7.60 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, +4.89 km, up to 1268 m off the optimal route, plus a 4 min 10 s stationary stop at a point 4918 m from pickup and 5158 m from drop-off [F4][F2]. That opens RD-1: no percentage or kilometre threshold is set, and any deviation not excused by RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 is an unexempted detour. No traffic excuse is available — the trace records no qualifying incident [F15] and the only bands on the corridor are band 4, far above the band 1–2 congestion bands (RD-4(b) does not exempt alone) [F13][F14][RD-4].

The rider did ask for a stop before the segment: at 17:33 she wrote "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes." and the driver replied "Sure" at 17:34, ahead of the 17:37:50 segment start [F9][F10][F4]. But the words name no road, no area and no outlet — they ask for a stop, not a route [F9]. RD-3(a) exempts a rider-named stop only where the rider named a specific place and the car stopped there; "a 7-Eleven on the way" names a kind, not a place, and the driver's own post-trip statement says he chose the outlet ("I went to the one I know") [F12][RD-3]. RD-3(b) is directly on point: a stop the rider asked for without naming a place, where the driver selected the location and created an off-route segment, does not exempt that segment's extra_km [RD-3]. RD-5 is likewise unavailable: what was agreed was a short stop (a "scope_other" kind of agreement), and a driver's statement of what the rider wanted is a claim, not rider consent [F12][RD-5]. The open question therefore resolves as counts on the ground the rider advocate named (scope_other); the driver's rider_named_stop reading fails on the words of F9 read with F12.

Amount: the trip is RydeTAXI, so excess metered mileage is chargeable [F5][F6][F8][RD-2]. Rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $29.53 ÷ 20.94 km = $1.4102/km [F8]. Unexempted extra_km on F4 = 4.89 km. 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.8959 → $6.90 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The waiting charge is not refunded: RydeTAXI waiting is metered and chargeable, and both advocates now concede it [F6][RD-3(c)].

No account flag: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the driver profile records route: 0, no-show: 0 with the single upheld dispute being of another kind, so the predicate is absent [F18][RD-6].

RD-3(a) does not exempt a stop whose place the rider did not name; RD-3(b) leaves the segment's extra_km counted when the driver's undisclosed chosen location creates the off-route segment; RD-5 consent here covers a short stop, not this 7.60 km loop reaching 1268 m off the optimal route [F4][RD-3][RD-5].

The driver's statement that he chose the outlet is a driver claim, not rider consent, and an undisclosed driver-chosen stop point that creates an off-route segment does not exempt that segment's extra_km [F12][F4][F9][RD-3][RD-5].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; no account flag on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeX is a non-metered service and the only disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7], so the fee stands only through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch, which routes a driver no-show claim to NS-1 [RD-? ] — concretely, NS-0 requires all of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) [F4][NS-0].

The first two elements are met and are not in dispute. NS-1(i): the trace and record show a driver tap ("I'm Here") at 14:14:10, not a platform auto-confirmation, and the platform separately logged arrival at 14:13:25 [F5][F6][NS-1]. NS-1(ii): at the tap the GPS placed the driver 41 m from the pickup, and the closest approach across the episode was 38 m, inside the 200 m radius [F1][F6][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) fails on the system records, which override the driver's later statements. After the 14:14:10 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 40 s (100 s), against the threshold of more than 3 minutes (180 s), until cancellation at 14:15:50 [F6][F4][NS-1]. The most generous alternative readings are still short: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 25 s, the platform arrival-to-cancellation gap was the same 2 min 25 s, and the stationary period at 41 m was 2 min 0 s [F2][F3][F5][NS-1]. The driver's in-app claim "3 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10] and his post-trip statement that he waited and cancelled as a no-show [F12] are contradicted by the timeline and cannot cure the shortfall [F4][F6][NS-1].

Because a driver-cancellation no-show charge requires all of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) and (iii) is unmet, the $6.61 has no charging ground and must be refunded in full (as a Ryde voucher, NS-7): the fee charged was $6.61 with 1.0× surge, so the refundable amount is $6.61, not a computed detour figure [F7][F8][NS-0][NS-2][NS-7].

The rider's request for an account-review flag is rejected. RD-6 attaches only where this case itself is upheld against the driver via a route-deviation finding (RD-2 refund or recorded RD-1 breach); here the trip was cancelled with no off-route segment, and NS-2's only flag condition — a fake "I'm Here" confirmation while not at the pickup — is not met, as the driver was 41 m from the pickup at the tap [F1][F6][F13][F14][F15][RD-2][RD-6][NS-2]. Profile facts are therefore not used to decide either way [F16][F17][RD-6].

Accepted as far as it states the rider's record is clean [F16], but a clean profile is not an element of NS-2 and cannot decide the fee either way; the refund rests on the failed NS-1(iii) wait, not on the rider's history [F16][F6][NS-2].
Correct that NS-1(i) is met by the driver tap at 14:14:10 [F6], but meeting (i) alone does not make the fee chargeable, since NS-1 requires (i)(ii)(iii) together [F6][NS-1].
Correct that NS-1(ii) is met (41 m at the tap, closest 38 m) [F1][F6], but this element alone does not establish the charge; the case turns on (iii), which fails [F6][NS-1].

The driver's profile (924 days, 4.53 rating, 815 trips in 90 d) [F17] cannot decide the no-show finding under NS-1/NS-2; the system records of the wait control, and they show the threshold unmet [F6][F2][F5][NS-1][NS-2].
Correctly conceded against the driver: the post-trip statement [F12] cannot cure the sub-three-minute wait measured by GPS and timeline [F6][F3].

ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute: the $6.61 cancellation fee stands as validly raised under NS-1; no refund and no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider was charged a $6.61 cancellation fee after the driver cancelled as a no-show [F4][F7]. NS-0 routes the fee to NS-1/NS-2 because `cancelled_by = driver` and the driver asserts the rider did not show [F4]. NS-1 requires (i) an arrival confirmation, (ii) the GPS placing the driver within the pickup range at the moment of that confirmation, and (iii) a continuous wait of more than 3 minutes at the pickup after the confirmation, until cancellation [NS-1]. The trace marks all three as settled ✓, and the facts bear that out: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 at 41 m from the pickup [F6], inside the 200 m data-layer radius, and the closest approach overall was 35 m [F1]. After the tap he stayed within 200 m of the pickup for 3 min 40 s and cancelled at 17:22:55 [F6][F4][F5], which exceeds the NS-1 default threshold of more than 3 minutes (3:01) [NS-1]. NS-2's $6.61 full refund therefore is not available, since none of (i)–(iii) failed [NS-2].

The rider's account that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is a statement only [F4]; the system record shows the driver first within 200 m at 17:17:50 and 5 min 5 s of cumulative time within 200 m before cancelling [F2][F3][F5], with the driver stationary 17:18:50–17:22:55 at 54 m from the pickup [F3]. No arrival by the rider appears anywhere in the record, so the fee was properly triggered [F2][F5][NS-1][NS-0].

No abuse of the "I'm Here" button arises on this record: the tap was inside the radius [F6], so the NS-2 flag trigger (m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200) is not met, and the trace records flag_account as not required [F6][NS-2]. The $6.61 is exactly Ryde's published cancellation fee with no surge component (1.0×), so there is no overcharge for FARE-1 to strip out [F7][F8][FARE-1]. Any refund would in any event be a Ryde voucher, not cash, and Ryde retains final discretion [NS-7].

Safety screen: I read all messages and the statement — the driver's arrivals notice and the cancellation notice are courteous and functional, and the complaint contains no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12]; nothing triggers SAFE-1 or SAFE-2. Evidence: the chat record is complete with both messages timestamped [F11] and the GPS trace covers the period up to cancellation without a hole [F2][F6], so the decisive elements are all settled on the record.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's complaint rests only on her unsupported statement that she came out a minute after cancellation [F4]; the system record shows the driver within 200 m since 17:17:50 and stationary 54 m away through the cancellation, with no rider arrival recorded [F2][F3][F5], so no full refund of the $6.61 can be founded and NS-2 does not apply [NS-2][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The fee in dispute is a rider-cancellation charge: cancelled_by = rider [F2], so the fee can only enter through NS-0's rider branch, which sends an on-demand booking to NS-4. NS-4 charges nothing where the rider cancels within 3 minutes of matching (≤ 3:00) and charges $6.61 only where the cancellation comes later. The timeline records acceptance at 18:23:00 and rider cancellation at 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s (150 s), and the fare record shows $6.61 actually charged [F2][F5]. On those settled values the charge fails its own precondition, so the whole $6.61 disputed item is refundable: refund_full of $6.61 [F5][F2][NS-0][NS-4].

The alternative basis for retaining the fee — a driver-side no-show — is also unavailable, though it is not needed. No arrival was ever recorded: driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1 (i) is not met, and the GPS record shows the driver's closest approach was 1816 m at 18:25:30 and that he never came within 200 m of the pickup, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) cannot be satisfied either [F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. With none of NS-1's conditions met, the fee cannot stand on that branch and NS-2's refund outcome follows [F3][F4][F1][NS-2].

The driver's written statement that he "was on his way when the rider cancelled" is consistent with the system records (no arrival ever recorded) and is not in genuine conflict with them, so nothing turns on the record-vs-statement priority here; it in any event cannot supply the NS-1 preconditions — a statement of being en route is not an arrival confirmation, and being en route is exactly what the records already show [F10][F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. His 18:24 chat message ("5 min more, traffic is slow") likewise describes a car still on the way, which the rider read and acted on [F8][F7].

Ryde's published rule gives no free-cancellation right merely because the driver is late or not yet arrived, and NS-4 says so expressly: lateness is not the rider's free-cancellation ground, and the rider's remedy for that is the NS-7 manual route [F1][F8][NS-4][NS-7]. Here the rider does not need it — the 3-minute rule alone decides the case, so the outcome does not depend on the driver's position.

No account flag arises. RD-6 requires an established case against the driver plus a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days; the driver's profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld (and the rider's the same), and the NS-2 add-on for tapping "I'm Here" while away from the pickup is not triggered because the driver never tapped at all [F15][F14][F4][RD-6][NS-2]. The structured flag field is therefore left false; the profile facts are used only to check the flag condition, not to decide the fee.

Evidence is sufficient: the timeline and fare records settle cancelled_by, the exact cancellation timing and the charged amount, the GPS record settles the driver's position, and the chat is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, all timestamped), so no record needed by NS-0/NS-4/NS-1 is missing [F2][F5][F1][F9].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement that he 'was on his way' [F10] is offered as neutral-to-supportive of retaining the fee, but it cannot support the charge: no arrival was ever recorded [F3][F4] and the GPS shows he never came within 200 m [F1], so NS-1's preconditions are unmet and the statement has no bearing on the outcome (NS-1). The advocate itself withdrew this point.

The driver's reply '5 min more, traffic is slow' [F8] is used to argue the rider knew the car was minutes away; that goes to the rider's expectation, not to liability. Ryde publishes no driver-late free-cancellation rule and lateness is not a basis to charge the rider either — the charge turns on the 3-minute timing rule (NS-4), which on F2 makes the fee unpayable.

The driver's clean 90-day record of 1043 trips and 0 upheld [F15] is invoked to deny any account action; that is accepted, but profile facts never decide the case itself and no flag is pressed here (RD-6, NS-2).

The rider's point that the driver was 1816 m away and never within 200 m [F1] is factually correct and checked, but it is not the ground of the ruling: the fee fails on the rider-cancellation branch under NS-4 on F2, and NS-1's position requirement is only an alternative ground (NS-1, NS-4).

The claim that NS-1 (iii) fails because the driver could not have waited 3 continuous minutes within 200 m [F1][F2] is correct and noted, but it is surplus to the outcome: NS-1 (i) already fails on F3/F4, and the refund rests on NS-4 (NS-1, NS-4).

The rider's reliance on the 3-minute window timing [F2] is accepted as decisive for NS-4; the added framing that the rider 'acted promptly once it was clear the driver was not near' is commentary and does not add an independent ground (NS-4).

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no account flag is warranted on this no-show claim
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case: the trip was cancelled by the driver [F4] on a driver-side no-show claim, so the $6.61 fee stands only through NS-1. The trace settles the first two conditions: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:35 [F6] and was 39 m from the pickup at that moment [F6][F1], so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are met — the rider advocate rightly conceded this [F6].

Condition NS-1 (iii) fails on the records. After the 13:02:35 tap the driver stayed continuously within 200 m of the pickup for only 2 min 55 s (175 s), and cancelled at 13:05:30 [F6][F4]; the required continuous wait is more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01, threshold 180 s), so the element is not satisfied [F6]. The driver advocate's answer is to measure from the earlier platform arrival at 13:01:00 (4 min 30 s before cancellation) [F2][F5], but NS-1 (iii) counts only waiting after the arrival confirmation, and the record itself ties the confirmation to the 13:02:35 tap [F6]; the pre-tap presence in the vicinity is expressly excluded [F2][F6]. The stationary window of 3 min 15 s at 40 m [F3] also begins at 13:02:15, 20 s before the tap [F6], and does not cure the shortfall.

The driver's own contemporaneous message is consistent with the records rather than curing them: at 13:05 he declared "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" [F10], yet the tap he relies on was at 13:02:35 [F6] — a driver's assertion of elapsed time is not a system record, and system records override statements [F12][F10][F6]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped but contains no rider message at all [F9][F10][F11], so neither side's account of when the rider emerged is settled by the record; that timing is not needed here because the fee already fails on NS-1 (iii) [F6].

With (iii) unmet, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 is refunded in full [F7][F4]. The published-fee and surge points [F7][F8] do not make the fee payable, since NS-0 lets it stand only through the NS-1 conditions.

No account flag: the flag condition in NS-2 (arrival confirmed while not at the pickup) is not met — the tap was inside the radius [F6][F1] — and RD-6 is not engaged because RD-2 refunds nothing on a no-show fee; the $6.61 is not a route-deviation refund. ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled trip recorded as a rider no-show, so the fee can only stand through NS-1, which the trace checks element by element [F4][NS-0]. The location elements pass: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:45 while 41 m from the pickup, and his closest approach was 3 m at 21:29:20, well inside the 200 m radius the trace applies [F6][F1][NS-1]. The waiting element fails: NS-1(iii) requires more than 3 minutes of continuous presence at the pickup after the arrival confirmation, and the trace measures only 105 s inside the radius after the tap, against a 180 s threshold [F6][NS-1]. The independent timeline figures agree — arrival recorded 21:28:35, cancellation at 21:31:30 two minutes 55 s later, cumulative time within 200 m 2 min 55 s [F5][F2][F4][NS-1]. Pre-tap time near the pickup is expressly not counted, so the 21:28:35–21:29:45 period cannot be added [F2][F6][NS-1].

The driver's post-trip statement that he waited at least 5 minutes is a statement, and the GPS and timeline records contradict it; system records govern the conflict [F12][F2][F6][NS-1]. His chat establishes presence and findability — an arrival ping with a vehicle description at 21:29, then "Cancelling, waited too long" at 21:31 — not that the required wait elapsed; the complete two-message log gives the rider no NS-1(iii) window to arrive [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

With NS-1(iii) unmet, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be returned in full [F7][F4][NS-2]. The refund is issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7, and the fee figure comes straight from the fare record, so no rate arithmetic is needed [F7][NS-7].

No account flag attaches: the trace found no fake arrival confirmation, and the tap was 41 m from the pickup, i.e. genuinely within the radius, so the NS-2 flag condition (arrival confirmed while not at pickup, m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200) is not met [F6][F1][NS-2]. The driver's profile (976 days, 1216 trips, 0 upheld disputes) is not used to decide the case and is not used for a flag [F17][NS-2].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint. They concern arrival, waiting and cancellation; nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. No escalation under SAFE-2 applies either.

Evidence status is sufficient: the trace confirms the GPS trace covers the wait with no hole from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation, and every element needed (who cancelled, tap distance, post-tap duration, fee charged) is settled by records [F2][F6][F4][F7][NS-1].

D3 relies on the driver's post-trip statement of a 5-minute wait, but a statement loses to the GPS/timeline records, which show 1 min 45 s inside 200 m after the tap and 2 min 55 s cumulative before cancellation; being findable is not waiting the required time [F12][F2][F6][NS-1].

D4 argues the complete timestamped chat helps the driver; the log in fact shows only an arrival ping at 21:29 and a cancellation notice at 21:31, leaving no NS-1(iii) window after the driver's own arrival confirmation [F11][F9][F10][NS-1].
