ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 22:42:00 after accepting at 22:33:00, and a $6.61 cancellation fee was applied [F3][F6]. Because the driver is the cancelling party and he asserts the rider no-showed, the fee only stands if NS-1 is satisfied: the arrival confirmation, the position at that moment, and more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting at the pickup [NS-0][NS-1].

Both NS-1 conditions fail on the system record. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while 1000 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup after the tap [F5]; his closest approach at any time was 873 m and he never came within 200 m [F1]; the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all [F4]. GPS and timeline records override the driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12], and that statement is contradicted point-for-point by the stationary window 1000 m away [F2] and by the cancellation timeline [F3] [NS-1].

With NS-1 unmet, the fee has no basis and the $6.61 cancellation fee on the record must be returned in full to the rider — for this fixed-fare RydeX trip the whole disputed charge is that fee [F6][NS-2][NS-7]. The rider's own presence cannot be system-verified (only her message at 22:38 [F9]); that fact cuts both ways but is irrelevant, since the charge fails on the driver's arrival conditions, not on whether the rider showed up [NS-1].

Separately, because the driver pressed the arrival button while GPS placed him 1000 m from the pickup point, this is an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, which calls for the account review add-on under NS-2; the driver's profile (2 of 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 d) is context only and does not decide anything [F5][F17][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Acceptance and cancellation times with the fee on record [F3][F6] only show the fee was applied, not that it was earned; NS-0 routes a driver-side no-show allegation into NS-1, whose conditions fail [F1][F5] [NS-0][NS-1].

The five-minute stationary window [F2] was spent 1000 m from the pickup after a tap made 1000 m out with 0 s inside 200 m [F5], so neither NS-1 (ii) nor (iii) is met; the driver withdrew this framing.
The rider's message that she was at the pickup [F9] is a statement without a GPS record locating her, and it does not cure the driver's missing arrival conditions [F1][F5] [NS-1].

The profile figures [F17] cannot decide the merits or convert a failed arrival into an operational error; profile facts never decide an issue alone, and the account action rests on the tap itself [F5] [NS-2].
With no speed band and no incident on the route in the trip window [F13][F14], 1.8 mm of light rain [F15] is not a reasonable cause under RD-4 for standing 1000 m away [RD-4].

The flag_account request is granted only through the NS-2 add-on for the false arrival confirmation [F5], not through RD-6: RD-6 also requires the driver's profile route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the rider's profile shows route: 0 upheld [F17] [RD-6][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Decline the refund request: inform the rider that the $6.61 cancellation fee was validly imposed under NS-1 (driver confirmed arrival in range at 18:24:35 and waited 3 min 50 s before cancelling), that Ryde has no weather or grace-period exception to the 3-minute no-show threshold, and that no account action attaches to this trip.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show fee case, so NS-0 routes it to NS-1: the fee stands only if (i) arrival was confirmed, (ii) the driver was within 200 m of the pickup at that moment, and (iii) he then stayed at the pickup continuously for more than 3 minutes until cancelling [F4][NS-0][NS-1]. The trace settles all three elements as ✓ and none of them is left for me to interpret; the only open item flagged is the SAFE-1 screen.

On (i) and (ii): the arrival confirmation is a driver tap, and at that tap (18:24:35) the driver was 41 m from the pickup point, inside the arrival radius, with the closest approach overall 38 m [F6][F1]. Both sides concede these elements in their rebuttals [F6][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; close the case and inform the rider that no refund is due.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider cancelled this on-demand RydeX trip herself at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance at 08:40:00, and the $6.61 cancellation fee is on record [F4][F7][NS-0]. NS-0 routes a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant booking through NS-4, and both advocates agree on that frame [F4][NS-0][NS-4].

NS-4 makes a rider cancellation free only within 3 minutes of matching; a cancellation after 3 minutes sustains the $6.61 fee [F4][NS-4]. The record shows 400 s, well beyond that window, so the fee stands and no refund is due [F4][F7][NS-4].

The rider's stated ground — "plans changed and the driver had not even arrived" — is contradicted by the system record: the driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:25 and stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 for 4 min 40 s [F1][F2][F3][NS-4]. NS-4 provides no relief for a driver who has not yet arrived, and here the driver had arrived; the rider's own message "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" confirms the cancellation was her change of mind, not a driver failure [F10][NS-4].

No separate refund trigger exists in the arrival/waiting record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m arrival radius), stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and the cancellation came 5 min 15 s after arrival [F5][F6][NS-1]. NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are therefore satisfied on the record and NS-2's refund condition is not engaged, so nothing turns on the no-show branch [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. The driver's post-trip statement that he was parked at the pickup is corroborated by the stationary GPS period and adds nothing either way [F3][F12][NS-1].

The fare record shows only the published $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge (1.0×) and no other add-on, so there is no unpublished charge to strike down under the fare rules [F7][F8][FARE-1]. Since no RD-1 route violation and no RD-2 refund arise in this no-show case, RD-6's flag condition is not met and no account flag is warranted [F5][F6][RD-6]. The parties' 90-day histories are background only and cannot decide the case [F16][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages and the driver's statement. Chat #1 is a neutral arrival notice and Chat #2 a polite apology with a cancellation notice; the driver's statement is a factual account of parking at the pickup [F9][F10][F12]. The screen is therefore "none".

Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete with every message timestamped, the timeline and GPS records cover acceptance, arrival, the stationary period and the cancellation instant, and the fare record carries the fee [F4][F5][F6][F7][F11]. No record needed to apply NS-0/NS-4 is missing, so there is no evidence gap and no reason to escalate.

ruling.reasoning:
The trip was cancelled by the driver at 09:54:25 with a $6.61 cancellation fee on record, so the fee only stands or falls under the NS-0 driver-cancellation branch [F4][F7][NS-0]. But the mandatory safety screen is not a fare question. Chat #3, sent by the driver at 09:54 — twenty-five seconds before he cancelled — reads: "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." I read that in context, not by keyword: it is not a pickup arrangement or a route remark; it is a conditional personal threat ("I will find you") aimed at the rider in response to her delay, in a chat record that is complete and fully timestamped, so there is no question of misquoting or of an unsent line [F12]. That is intimidation of the other party, which Ryde's code of conduct bars as "abuse of any kind", and it falls squarely within SAFE-1 [F11][F12][SAFE-1]. [F11][F4]. ruling.reasoning:
WHAT HAPPENED. A RydeX trip Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall, pickup 17:08, drop-off 17:31, fixed fare $32.86. At 17:09 the rider messaged "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F5], so the two messages are the whole exchange. The driver's written statement, made after the trip and not part of the chat, adds "The rider tried to open the door at the lights. I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on." [F6]. The rider's complaint is that the driver threatened to lock her in and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride.

WHAT IS DISPUTED. The meaning of F4 read with F3 — a request to be let out immediately followed by a conditional "or I lock the doors" — is contested: the rider reads it as a threat/intimidation of a passenger who asked to leave a moving vehicle; the driver reads it as a safety instruction tied to the rider attempting to open a door [F3][F4][F6]. This is exactly the kind of semantic judgement SAFE-1 reserves to a human reading: the system must screen, not auto-decide, and the screen here is engaged [SAFE-1].

SAFETY SCREEN. I read every chat message, the complaint and the driver's statement. The complaint alleges being kept in the car ("threatened to lock me in ... felt unsafe for the whole ride"), and F4 is on its words a confinement ultimatum aimed at the rider right after she asked to alight [F3][F4][F6]. Given the asymmetric screen — a missed threat that lets a case auto-execute is not acceptable, and a false "suspected" merely costs a human look — I record this as "suspected" and decline to rule [SAFE-1]. The record also carries a detention-of-passenger / unsafe-ride allegation, which falls to the human reviewer under the safety-incident branch [SAFE-2].

WHY NO MONEY MOVES. The dispute is a safety incident, and the trace settles that a safety complaint permits only escalation. Independently, there is nothing to refund: actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km) [F1], duration +1.9 min [F2], and the fare is a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86, so under the non-metered branch no mileage-driven excess arises and no refund formula is available [RD-1][RD-2]; the rider's stop request [F3] was never agreed by the rider-side counterpart and no change-of-destination charge was added, so nothing to waive there either [FARE-1]. Amount is therefore null.

WHAT THE REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK: (1) whether F4, in context, is intimidation/abuse of a passenger rather than a safety instruction, and whether F6's safety gloss can be reconciled with the car continuing to Bedok Mall (F1); (2) the rider's account of what happened between 17:10 and drop-off, since the chat shows no further message from either party [F5] and F1/F2 say nothing about whether the car was stopped or moving at 17:09; (3) whether the rider attempted to open a door while moving, which F6 asserts but no gps/timeline fact records. Note the driver's profile (893 d, 4.62, 1038 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld) [F8] and the rider's clean profile [F7] are background only and do not decide this case [RD-6].

The chat is complete and timestamped [F5] but the meaning of F4 and what occurred during the remaining ride are for a human to determine; a safety case takes no automatic ruling [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. No monetary adjustment is available: fixed RydeX fare $32.86, 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2].

Under the system-record-over-statement rule the driver's safety gloss in F6 cannot resolve the meaning of F4 [SAFE-1].

Correct that RD-6's flag condition is not met — the driver's profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F8] and the rider-side no longer seeks an account flag; profile facts cannot decide the route or safety question either way [RD-6]. This does not dispose of the SAFE-1 screening, which is independent of RD-6.

Accepted in substance by both sides and not in issue: the case is referred to a human under SAFE-1 [SAFE-1]. I do not adopt the rider's further submission that a finding against the driver follows; the referral is a screening outcome, not a finding [F4][F6].

ruling.recommended_action: Decline the refund request; keep the $6.61 cancellation fee as charged and inform the rider of the voucher/appeal route under NS-7.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a driver-cancellation with a rider-no-show allegation, so it enters only through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver ([F4]) and the driver's basis for cancelling was non-appearance ([F11], [F13]), which routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 [NS-0]. The $6.61 charged is the published cancellation fee on the record ([F7]) and no surge applied ([F8]), so the only question is whether the NS-1 conditions were met.

All three NS-1 elements are settled by the trace and the records. Arrival confirmation (i): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 ([F6]); the trace marks this confirmed by driver_tap, not by platform auto-detection, and the earlier platform arrival at 14:03:20 ([F5]) does not substitute for the tap requirement [NS-1]. Position at the tap (ii): the GPS placed the car 178 m from the pickup at the tap moment ([F6]), inside the 200 m arrival radius applied by the data layer (the radius is a data-layer parameter, not a policy threshold), and the car had been within 200 m since 14:03:20 with a closest approach of 40 m ([F2], [F1]) — so the rider's C1/C2 argument that 178 m "fails" (ii) is an argument against the radius itself, not against the record [NS-1]. Continuous wait after the tap (iii): F6 records 220 s (3 min 40 s) continuously inside the radius after the tap, above the NS-1 default of more than 3 minutes; the GPS trace covering the wait has no hole, and the car was stationary from 14:05:55 to the 14:09:55 cancellation ([F3]) [NS-1]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped ([F12]), so the sequence can be read directly: the driver gave his position and vehicle at 14:06 ([F9]), the rider said at 14:07 she was at the entrance and could not see him ([F10]), and the driver cancelled at 14:09 after noting he had waited more than 3 minutes ([F11]) [NS-1]. The rider's F10 message is her own statement of where she was, not a GPS record, and it is consistent with the measured facts: the car was not at the entrance, but it was within the arrival radius the policy contemplates [NS-1].

Because (i), (ii) and (iii) all hold, NS-2 is not triggered: there is no element failure to justify a refund of the $6.61 [NS-2]. The driver's written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes ([F13]) is a self-serving post-trip claim (G11) and I do not use it — it is unnecessary, because the GPS and timeline records independently satisfy the elements [NS-1]. Traffic facts ([F14], [F15]) and weather ([F16]) are irrelevant to a no-show fee. On NS-7 the rider's dispute is timely ([F4], [F5]), but NS-7 governs only the form and window of a refund once one is due; since no fee waiver or refund condition is met, no voucher issues [NS-7]. The ride-hailing fairness point that the driver parked 179 m from the pin ([F3]) while the rider stood at the entrance ([F10]) is a service-quality matter the rider can raise with RydeHELP, but on this record the fee was chargeable and the complaint fails.

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages ([F9], [F10], [F11]), the rider's complaint text and the driver's statement ([F13]). Message F11 ("Waited more than 3 min, cancelling") is a factual cancellation notice, F10 is a rider searching for the car, and F9 gives vehicle and location; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the record. Finding: none [SAFE-1].

Evidence: the record settles every element this ruling needs — the arrival tap and its GPS distance, the continuous in-radius wait with no trace hole, the cancellation time, and the amount charged — so the evidence is sufficient and no gap is named [NS-1], [NS-2]. The rider advocate withdrew the flag_account limbs (C5, C6) and RD-6 is not engaged in any event because the driver is not held in breach here [RD-6].

Standing 179 m from the pin while remaining inside the arrival radius is what NS-1 (ii)/(iii) measure; the policy requires position within the arrival area, not the rider's entrance (F3, F6) [NS-1]. The rider's F10 message is her statement, not a GPS record.

The driver did communicate his position and vehicle at 14:06 before the rider's 14:07 message (F9, F10), and the record shows he then stayed inside the radius a further 3 min 40 s before cancelling at 14:09 (F6, F11); 'no reply' does not negate the measured wait (F3, F6) [NS-1].
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are satisfied (F6, F5, F12), NS-2 is not triggered and no full refund arises; the $6.61 is the published cancellation fee (F7, F8) [NS-2].
Withdrawn by the rider in rebuttal; and the tap at 178 m (F6) is inside the arrival radius, so there is no abuse-of-button basis under NS-2 (F6) [NS-2].

The conclusion (NS-1 (ii) satisfied) is correct, but D3 rests on the 200 m data-layer radius alone while the trace settles (ii) on F6's measured 178 m; the radius is an implementation parameter and I do not cite it as a policy threshold (F6) [NS-1].

The rider's 14:07 message (F10) does not by itself show she was not at the pickup point — she states she was at the entrance; the no-show finding rests on the measured in-radius wait and the completed three-element test, not on that message (F10, F6, F3) [NS-1].

The trip is a metered RydeTAXI Jurong Point → Suntec City, 30.0 km against a 24.4 km optimal route (+5.6 km) and 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate, charged $60.30 on the meter [F1][F2][F7]. Under RD-1 every off-route segment must be individually checked against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and only an unexempted segment is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2]. The trace confirms exactly one off-route segment, F3 (13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, up to 1391 m off corridor) [F3].

RD-4 gives no cover: the trace marks (a) failed and the record shows no traffic incident near the route in the trip window [F15], while the only speed-band evidence is AER band 2 for 12:41–13:07, which stops exactly as the segment begins and is, per RD-4(b)/G3, insufficient on its own to exempt a segment [F12][F3][RD-4].

The decisive question is RD-5 consent: the driver asked at 13:03 whether to take another way because traffic on the AER was building up, and the rider replied at 13:04 "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" — both messages timestamped in a complete two-message record, i.e. before the segment began at 13:07 [F8][F9][F10]. That is a general route choice, not consent to a named road: F8 names only the road to be avoided and no rider message names a road to be taken, so no named-road tie exists to trigger G13 [F8][F9]. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination and excludes only the driver's own affairs — a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing; here no stop, errand or detour-specific purpose of the driver's own appears anywhere in the record, so the loop does not fall within that carve-out and the segment is exempt [F9][F3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not rider consent, and is not needed [F11][RD-5].

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, no unexempted segment remains for RD-2, and the metered excess (billed as $7.88, 5.59 km × $1.4101/km) is not refundable [F4][F7][RD-2]. The other line items are untouched: the $0.11 is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit (0.4 min × $0.26/min), which RD-3(c) keeps with the driver and which the rider does not claim, no surge applied (multiplier 1.0×), and the $1.47 platform fee is a published fee — none generates a refund [F5][F6][F7][RD-3][FARE-1]. RD-6 does not attach: no RD-1 breach is recorded and the driver's 90-day route-upheld count is 0 [F18][RD-6]. Amount is therefore $0.00, i.e. no_action.
